# sentry_project_team (Resource)

Gives one more team access to a project. The team a project is created under is managed by `sentry_project.team_id`; do not declare that one here as well.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sentry_team" "sre" {
  name = "SRE"
}

# Give a second team access to a project. The project's own team is set by
# sentry_project.team_id.
resource "sentry_project_team" "api_sre" {
  project_id = sentry_project.api.id
  team_id    = sentry_team.sre.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) ID of the project, e.g. `sentry_project.example.id`. A project slug works too and is kept as written, but it stops resolving when the project is renamed, so prefer the ID.
- `team_id` (String) ID of the team, e.g. `sentry_team.example.id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<team_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <project slug or ID>/<team slug or ID>.
terraform import sentry_project_team.api_sre api/sre
```
